doors.note: Configured page (WordPress + The Events Calendar). Static curl: the page links its own feeds — <link> to /calendarofevents/?ical=1 and https://eagle-ny.com/wp-json/tribe/events/v1/ — which is how the crawler adopts the REST door (🚪 MACHINE DOOR). Its HTML list was not enumerated; the REST feed is the same data with venue, url, image, cost and description as fields.

Server default window start_date=2026-09-18 05:00:00 → end_date=2028-09-20 04:59:59, status=publish. Rows carry start_date/end_date as local wall clock with timezone "America/New_York", venue { venue: "The Eagle NYC", city, state } (no street address), url (the event page on eagle-ny.com), description (mostly empty), image (mostly false), cost (mostly empty), categories []. No recurrence fields: every night, including the nightly DJ sets and weekly socials, is its own row.

recon.notes: Recon from one cached read of each door on 2026-09-19. 453 rows across 10 REST pages, 47 distinct titles, 2026-09-18 → 2028-09-19. The bar posts every DJ night as a dated row two years ahead.

coverage.basis: Feed door: The Events Calendar REST route, 10 pages × 50 = 453 rows (total 453 reconciles), all future from the server's default start. Every row is a single: the feed states no recurrence (no series route, no rrule keys). 346 rows start after the 2026-12-18 horizon and are documented with expect.extracted "unknown" — the reader keeps one-offs past the horizon but drops repeating titles' far rows. The listing HTML was not enumerated separately: the parser adopts this feed as its door.
